# Orbit Store (Beta)

> A modern PS5 download manager with resumable downloads, a native TV app, browser controls and the Orbit Zero desktop companion.

The official project is https://github.com/saawant12/orbit-store-ps5. Orbit Store has no official social media accounts. It is free to use, and nothing is locked behind a payment. Optional contributions help cover development tools, test hardware and servers. The only official donation page is https://buymeacoffee.com/saawant12.

The latest published release is Orbit Store 1.8.1, with native TV app 1.12.1 and Orbit Zero 1.8.1. It lets games and files be copied, moved or changed while downloads run, lets Zero send games while the PS5 downloads, reuses the least recently used pairing slot when all are taken, fetches USB download pieces from the provider’s storage after the first redirect, and saves Zero pairing on Linux window managers. Orbit 1.8.0 added reorganised settings, 26 interface languages, automatic PS5 shutdown, file choices when clearing download history and drive changes for computer-managed transfers. Update the components you use from the same release; the native app and download service have separate version numbers. PPSA99177.ffpkg already includes the matching service, and Zero also includes an ELF it can upload. A separate ELF download is only needed for a separately managed service copy. Stop an older running service before starting its replacement; installing a package does not replace that running process.

## LZ4 and the 1.7.5 update

Browse → Format → LZ4 is available in the browser/ELF, native PS5 app and Orbit Zero, in all four interfaces. The catalogue includes 49 LZ4 options across 48 PS5 games. LZ4 describes game assets, separately from the outer ZIP/RAR/7z archive. Orbit extracts that archive and preserves the LZ4 assets; it does not recursively decompress them or convert them into other game formats. Packaging filters still match. Source classification does not establish runtime, firmware or loader compatibility. See guides/downloads.md#lz4-games.

Release 1.7.5 improves partial-download recovery and recognises an original remounted drive using its saved marker or the job’s own partial file. TorBox downloads use at most eight connections per game and respect cooldowns; Zero waits at least five minutes when the download server refuses a connection before any data arrives. Removed sources require another option. Library moves copy, read back and verify files, then register the new location with compatible ShadowMount before removing the original. Supported firmware requirements discovered after extraction appear in Downloads and installation review. Zero also fixes EISDIR completion errors on exFAT drives and upload/launch through Payload Manager 0.6.3, and falls back to its bundled catalogue if the saved copy is missing or unreadable.

## PS4 and PS5 games

Orbit’s current catalogue contains 2,157 games: 1,181 PS5 games and 976 PS4 games, with 4,997 single-file download options from Archive.org, Vikingfile and AkiraBox. Formats include FFPFSC, exFAT, LZ4, PKG, FPKG, ZIP, RAR and 7z. Sources are opt-in; available formats depend on the game. Supported archives extract automatically on the selected PS5 drive, or on the computer before Orbit Zero transfers the extracted files. Compressed size and extracted space requirements differ. Known source passwords, including pippo, are tried automatically; custom-password retries reuse the downloaded archive.

PS4 support starts with service/browser version 1.1.0, native app 1.4.0 and Orbit Zero 1.1.0; these are minimum versions, not the current release. Browse has a Platform filter for PS4, PS5 or All platforms. PS4 CUSA and PS5 PPSA editions remain separate, with their own metadata and download choices. PS4 options include single-file .pkg packages, labelled PKG or FPKG, and single ZIP, RAR or 7z archives. Archive support requires 1.2.0 or later; use the latest matching apps. Saving or extracting a package does not install it automatically. The 1.5.0 and later apps provide an explicit Install on PS5 action; earlier versions need a compatible package installer. A platform label does not imply a frame-rate patch, DLC or universal compatibility. Orbit's ELF and TV app run on PS5, not PS4 consoles.

Discover opens first. Store presents New on Orbit before Latest releases and an All games grid; Crossbar, Cinema and Panorama arrange these collections differently. New on Orbit shows up to 40 games: curated highlights first, with remaining places filled by recent catalogue additions ordered by game release date. Discover’s All games, Browse and Library load more items as you scroll. Browse supports platform, source, format, region and size filters, search, sorting and shared favourites. In native Browse and Discover, Square toggles Favourite in Store; Triangle does so in Crossbar, Cinema and Panorama. Controller shortcuts and section navigation depend on the interface.

New games and metadata corrections arrive through catalogue updates. App settings → Game catalogue → Refresh catalogue checks manually. The last available catalogue is cached for offline browsing, and existing downloads keep their chosen file identity. Older apps receive only data their version supports; some older feeds retain their last compatible revision when the newer catalogue exceeds their capacity. Refreshing alone does not add app features such as PS4 browsing, DLC or installation.

Store is the default interface. Appearance also offers Crossbar, Cinema and Panorama across the native app, browser and Orbit Zero. Select Keep within the 15-second confirmation to save a choice; Switch back or the timeout restores the previous interface. Preferences are separate for each app/browser and do not change the queue, favourites or download settings. All interfaces offer Full or Reduced motion. Crossbar has time-of-day ribbon backgrounds, Cinema has blurred art or plain black behind menus, and Panorama has four accent colours and faint art or plain black behind pages.


## Install and use Orbit Store

Orbit requires a PS5 environment capable of running homebrew ELF payloads. Firmware, loader and ShadowMount compatibility vary. Run orbit_store.elf through a payload manager or ELF loader, then open the Orbit Store browser shortcut in the Media tab. The native PPSA99177.ffpkg goes in /data/homebrew/ and opens from the Games row using kstuff and ShadowMountPlus. This native app package is separate from downloaded game packages.

The native app bundles Orbit's service. A compatible ELF loader on port 9021 lets it start the service. Uploading or installing a new copy does not replace an already-running session. In 1.5.0, Update Orbit updates the TV app and service together. Open native App settings → Updates & startup, browser App settings → Updates & startup in Store, or Settings → Updates & startup in the other browser layouts. With a local ELF loader on port 9021, Orbit restarts the service and resumes downloads interrupted by that restart. Restart Orbit restarts only the service. Orbit updates the detected native installation location. Close and reopen the TV app after updating it, then check its running version; saving the image does not activate it. If port 9021 is unavailable, start the saved or synced ELF through Payload Manager or the usual launcher. Older versions still need separate update and manual restart steps; check the running version afterward. Pairing and the queue stay saved.

Phone and computer browser controls use http://<ps5-ip>:34177/ on the local network. Pair devices displays the console's six-digit code; Show code on PS5 repeats the notification. Keep codes private and the service on a trusted local network.

Enable the providers you want in Sources & accounts settings and save your selection, including AkiraBox when updating from an earlier release. Choose a game, source and drive in Download options. Direct downloads run on PS5. Provider pages open on PS5 while preserving the selected game, source and destination. For both Vikingfile and AkiraBox on the current matching PS5 apps, complete verification and wait without pressing Download. Orbit captures the ready link and returns to the browser or native app automatically. A paired phone controls this flow but does not host the provider browser. Orbit validates the selected file before queueing it.

Archive.org sign-in is available in native/browser App settings → Sources & accounts → Archive.org and Orbit Zero’s Settings → Sources & accounts. The PS5 apps share the console session; Zero keeps a separate session on the computer. Passwords are not saved. Sign-in can unlock account-required files, but cannot restore removed files. Release 1.3.5 removed 225 unavailable Archive.org options.

Optional TorBox delivery is configured in browser App settings → Sources & accounts → TorBox with the user's own API key. Orbit Zero also supports computer-side TorBox in Settings → Sources & accounts; its account is separate from the console account. Supported hosts, account plans, quotas and file-size limits apply. Original-provider downloads remain available. A TorBox job is never silently changed to direct delivery.

Downloads supports pause, resume, cancellation, retry and queue ordering. Finished contains completed downloads; cancelled items have their own view. History removal offers Keep files or reviewed deletion, including bulk actions. Previews show actual paths and sizes. A remembered preference can be reset to Ask every time under Storage & cleanup → Removing download history. Files in use are protected, deletion failures retain the entry, and installed games are not uninstalled. Delete download can remove a cancelled job and its partial file after confirmation. Keep the PS5 awake during downloads; rest-mode downloading is not supported.

Completed downloads handled by Orbit Store show their saved file or extracted folder path under Downloads → Finished → Location in both the browser and native app. This records the save location, not a fresh check that the file exists or is installed. Orbit Zero download details show the full PS5 destination path and the computer path while a cached copy remains. Both routes save to the selected PS5 drive's homebrew folder.

Library reads installed games and drive sources from a compatible ShadowMount v1 local API, supplementing installed PKG games omitted by older ShadowMount versions with on-console inventory. Inventory, drive information and game sizes refresh automatically. Compatible Files changes and newly connected drives trigger a bounded scan; Scan for games remains a manual fallback. Mount/unmount and copy/move depend on provider and format support. A completed file is not necessarily installed or launchable. Orbit does not launch or uninstall games.

Support Orbit is an optional settings entry in the refreshed 1.7.5 packages. Native and browser: App settings → Support Orbit (Settings → Support Orbit in other layouts). Zero Store: Settings → Support Orbit; other layouts: Settings → Support Orbit. The native app shows a QR code and opens the selected official link; the browser and Zero offer Open support page and Show QR code. Support options come from the official public .github/FUNDING.yml, with the last valid list or bundled official link available if it cannot refresh.

## Other current features

Version 1.6.0 adds phone/computer notifications through ntfy, with server/topic credentials and event choices in App settings → Notifications. It supports 1–64 connections per download (default eight); concurrent PS5 downloads share a 64-connection budget. Browse supports multiple sources/formats, hiding installed or saved games, and tags: PlayStation exclusive, Local co-op, Split-screen, Open world, Story-driven, Soulslike, PSVR supported and PSVR2 supported. PlayStation exclusives exclude official PC/Xbox/Nintendo editions; VR tags include optional support. Tag coverage is curated and not exhaustive. Completed Zero downloads keep readable filenames with collision-safe numbering.

Other changes in 1.5.0: known firmware requirements on download options, with incompatible choices warned and sorted last rather than blocked; Zero remembers the last paired firmware until unpairing. PS5 download completion/failure notifications have an on/off setting. Update Orbit installs the TV app and service together, then the service can restart through a local ELF loader on port 9021 and resume interrupted downloads; Restart Orbit is also available. Native Diagnostics & about → Save diagnostic report and Zero Settings → Diagnostics & about → Export log save private-data-free reports locally. Zero adds per-stage ETA and transfer read-ahead.

## DLC and Add-ons

DLC support is available in 1.5.0. The add-on catalogue has 626 add-ons (528 PS4 and 98 PS5), 628 download options and 192 associated base games. These counts are separate from game counts and base-game download options.

Add-ons follows Browse in navigation across browser, native PS5 and Zero in Store, Crossbar, Cinema and Panorama. Add-ons (count) on game details opens the collection filtered to that base game. Search matches add-on and base-game names; filters include Platform, Type, Source and Region, with Recently added as the default order. Tiles identify the add-on, base game and type; artwork falls back to the base game.

Types are Expansion, Content pack, Activation package and Bundle. Activation packages unlock content already present in the base game rather than containing it. Details show known contents, required base-game edition/title ID and version requirements. Unknown requirements or a missing/mismatched base game produce a warning without blocking the download. A title-ID match alone never establishes compatibility. Seeing a base game in Library does not mark its DLC installed.

Add-ons reuse download options, source accounts, supported TorBox delivery, extraction, transfer and recovery. Zero can download DLC to This computer without a PS5 and send it later. Download labels retain base-game and add-on identity. Installation follows the explicit Install on PS5 flow; users select individual packages from bundles. Orbit does not install every package automatically, fetch game updates or choose installation order. The v8 feed keeps games and add-ons in separate collections; v7 and older feeds contain compatible base-game data only.

## Game installation

Use the current Orbit client and matching running PS5 service; a catalogue refresh alone does not enable installation. After download or transfer to PS5, Downloads → Downloaded files or Install on PS5 opens package selection. Users explicitly install each PKG/FPKG, including individual packages in DLC bundles. The PS5 chooses its configured installation storage. Downloaded PKG/FPKG files are kept by default; 1.6.0 adds optional deletion after confirmed successful installation in App settings → Storage & cleanup → Installed packages. Failed installations and changed files are retained. Installation progress is separate from download and transfer progress. A completed computer PKG/FPKG can use Zero’s Stream & install to serve it directly to the PS5 installer, or Send to PS5 followed by Install on PS5. Orbit does not launch games or change firmware/licence compatibility.

Newly completed exFAT, FFPFSC, compatible .ffpkg images and extracted game folders automatically request a ShadowMount scan when its compatible local API is running. Orbit checks inventory before confirming registration. If ShadowMount was unavailable, users can start it and choose Scan with ShadowMount in the download details. Orbit does not launch ShadowMount or change its configuration. Old completed downloads are not all rescanned on upgrade. Check installation reconciles uncertain installation status; Orbit does not automatically resubmit an uncertain installation.

## Orbit Zero for desktop

Orbit Zero supports macOS, Windows and Linux on ARM64 and x64. Choose Save to → This computer to download without a paired or connected PS5. A completed download offers Show in folder and Send to PS5. Connect and pair the console when ready to send; the saved computer copy is kept. For uncompressed files, a computer downloads and transfers completed chunks to PS5 over the local network, using Wi-Fi or Ethernet. Archives finish downloading and extracting on the computer before their files transfer. The PS5 does not need internet for this route; the computer needs provider access for new downloads. Before transferring to PS5, start the console's jailbreak and Payload Manager or ELF loader, or its matching Orbit service.

Console → Start Orbit on PS5 can upload the compatible receiver ELF, then connect for pairing. Zero reconnects to the saved console when reopened. Computer is the default download route; Prefer PS5 checks whether the console can reach the source. Native App settings → Devices → Orbit Zero enables computer queue controls on PS5. Downloads shows computer download and PS5 transfer progress separately. PS4 packages use these same controls.

Vikingfile downloads first use the saved account session to request a matching direct link. If verification is needed, Vikingfile opens in a separate computer browser window for Zero downloads. In Zero 1.4.0 or later, users complete verification and wait without pressing Download; Zero captures the matching ready link and closes the provider window. Unwanted popups are blocked; Back, Reload and Return to download page restore navigation. Provider sessions persist separately from the main application. AkiraBox users complete verification and wait without pressing Download: Orbit captures the ready link. The PS5 browser returns to Orbit automatically after queueing; the matching native app closes its provider window automatically, and Zero closes its provider window.

Zero Settings → Downloads contains simultaneous computer downloads, connections, retries and route preference. Storage & cleanup contains the computer folder and cache cleanup. One game downloads at a time by default; users can choose 1–8 in Orbit Store or Orbit Zero. One file transfers to PS5 at a time while computer downloads continue. Automatic cleanup is off by default and removes completed computer copies only after a confirmed PS5 transfer. Clear completed cache removes completed copies while retaining PS5 files and unfinished downloads. The computer's credential store protects saved pairing.

Delete archives after extracting is separate from completed-cache cleanup and is on by default. It is in Orbit Store's App settings → Storage & cleanup and Zero's Settings → Storage & cleanup. It removes the archive after successful extraction, retaining it on extraction errors for retry. Zero's extracted files follow the Computer cache preference, whose automatic removal is off by default. Both the archive and extracted files need space until extraction succeeds.

After a disconnection, reconnect the original PS5 and destination, keep partial files, and choose Resume. If its IP address changed, update Settings → Devices → Connection settings; Zero verifies the saved pairing. If pairing was reset, Pair again and keep downloads requires confirmation and a fresh PS5 code. Resume verifies the existing PS5 partial against the computer copy and continues from the verified position when possible. If it cannot resume safely, Zero offers an explicit choice to delete the old partial and start over; it never silently discards the partial. Restart PS5 transfer can reuse the saved computer copy when offered. Cancel and remove partials discards unfinished files after confirmation. Stop transfer keeps remaining files and frees the queue after the receiver confirms the stop, but that transfer cannot resume afterward. For an existing receiver transfer, reconnect the console before cancelling or stopping; failed confirmation leaves the operation available to retry.

Orbit Store App settings → Downloads → Download recovery and Zero Settings → Downloads → Download recovery configure separate console/computer retry settings. Automatic retries allows 0–10 (default 3), with 0 disabling them. The default retry delay is 10 seconds; a download below 1 KiB/s for 60 seconds is treated as stalled. Changes apply on the next attempt, and providers can require longer waits.

Refresh download link for a computer download works while the PS5 is disconnected. Zero verifies the selected file before reusing partial data; reconnect the PS5 to transfer it.

Orbit Zero retries temporary computer-download failures with fewer connections; deliberate pauses, changed files, access restrictions and disk failures are not retried indefinitely. Remove from Downloads offers to keep files or review and delete the computer and/or PS5 copies. It preserves the entry when deletion fails and does not delete files still in use. Recover downloads → Review PS5 transfer can release an orphaned blocking transfer after confirmation. Recover downloads → Choose file also restores a completed file under its saved game name, or an older .cache file. Keep the name and folder Orbit used; a named file needs its completion record on this computer. Review the matching download and destination, add to queue, then Resume. Size alone does not prove an older cache is complete, and an already-deleted cache cannot be recovered.

Updates checks for new desktop versions automatically, downloads the matching OS/architecture package, verifies its SHA-256 digest and opens it only when requested. Zero never replaces or restarts itself automatically. Mac packages are Developer ID signed but not notarized; Windows and Linux packages are unsigned. Use the installation guide for permissions and package choices.

## Shutdown and destination changes

Automatic PS5 shutdown is off by default. In native/browser Downloads settings or Zero Settings → Downloads, enable it and choose All downloads or a PS5 job under Wait for. The per-download Shut down when finished action confirms the choice, shows “Automatic shutdown scheduled.” and changes to “Cancel automatic shutdown”. A selected job does not override other unfinished work. Downloads, transfers and installations must finish; paused/failed work, pending installation checks, file operations, updates and a disconnected busy Zero computer block it. Installation failure cancels the schedule. A 60-second countdown can be cancelled from any connected client. Keep Zero open while it has unfinished work. Old completed history does not trigger shutdown after a restart. This turns off the PS5, not the computer, and is not rest-mode downloading.

Zero checks computer space and shows PS5 free space, queued transfers and projected space. It blocks known insufficient destinations and checks unknown extraction sizes after inspection. A usable preferred drive is kept; otherwise a suitable roomier drive is suggested. Explicit selections are not silently changed. Change drive applies to computer-managed transfers with a retained computer copy, including completed transfers. It restarts only the transfer to the newly selected PS5 drive, without downloading again. Completed files on the original PS5 drive remain. Optional old-partial deletion needs explicit consent and receiver verification. Direct PS5 downloads do not use this action.

## Settings

Settings organisation: Orbit Store uses App settings in the default layout and Settings in other layouts. Zero has Settings in all four layouts. Categories are Downloads; Storage & cleanup; Sources & accounts; Devices; Appearance; Notifications (PS5); Game catalogue; Updates & startup; Diagnostics & about; Support Orbit. Zero labels computer and PS5 scope, and its Downloads gear opens Downloads settings. Console remains a status overview. See guides/settings.md. The interface supports 26 languages, including Arabic RTL and Japanese, Chinese and Korean fonts.

## Languages and support

Orbit Store and Orbit Zero support English, Arabic, Czech, Danish, Dutch, Finnish, French, German, Greek, Hungarian, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Norwegian Bokmål, Polish, Portuguese (Brazil), Portuguese (Portugal), Romanian, Russian, Spanish, Swedish, Turkish, Ukrainian, Simplified Chinese and Traditional Chinese. Native App settings → Appearance → Language chooses a language, or Automatic follows the PS5 language. Browser App settings → Appearance → Language sets the device preference. Zero's globe-shaped Language control in Store, or Settings → Appearance → Language in the other layouts, chooses a language or follows System language. Game metadata and provider pages may retain their original language.

Diagnostics are available locally in browser App settings → Diagnostics & about and native App settings → Diagnostics & about. Both can display and save a report to a PS5 drive; Zero Settings → Diagnostics & about → Export log saves a desktop report and includes PS5 diagnostics when connected. Reports exclude pairing codes, access tokens, download links, game names and paths, and are not sent automatically. Bug reports should identify the app and version, game platform/title ID, source, format, destination and failing stage. Display or navigation reports should also name the interface and input method.

Payload-manager integration and automatic startup are opt-in. Orbit leaves the manager's global Autoload switch unchanged. Keep the console awake during transfers. Physical-console compatibility and game installation depend on the user's setup.

Orbit Store is GPL-3.0-or-later. Releases provide the complete source corresponding to the PS5 service and native app, copyleft dependency sources, licence notices and rebuild instructions. Desktop packages include their dependency notices. Use third-party content only when entitled to obtain and use it; Orbit is independent of Sony, publishers and download providers.

## Downloads

- [Current release](https://github.com/saawant12/orbit-store-ps5/releases/latest): Version, changelog, installation instructions, source archives and licence bundle.
- [Current ELF](https://github.com/saawant12/orbit-store-ps5/releases/latest/download/orbit_store.elf): The Orbit application payload.
- [Native TV app](https://github.com/saawant12/orbit-store-ps5/releases/latest/download/PPSA99177.ffpkg): The Games-row app, including the Orbit service.
- [TV app SHA-256 checksum](https://github.com/saawant12/orbit-store-ps5/releases/latest/download/PPSA99177.ffpkg.sha256): Verify the FFPKG before installing.
- [ELF SHA-256 checksum](https://github.com/saawant12/orbit-store-ps5/releases/latest/download/orbit_store.elf.sha256): Verify the downloaded payload before loading it.
- [Payload Manager feed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/saawant12/orbit-store-ps5/main/payloads.json): Add this URL in Payload Manager under Settings, Manage Sources, Add Source. The feed contains Orbit's ELF URL, version and checksum.

## Support

- [Issues](https://github.com/saawant12/orbit-store-ps5/issues): Report problems with the Orbit version, PS5 firmware, loader and steps to reproduce. Keep pairing codes and private information out of reports.

## Files, saved filters and Vikingfile accounts

Version 1.7.0 adds Library → Files in all three clients, shared saved Browse/Add-ons filters, automatic Library scans and size measurements, Vikingfile sessions and computer-to-PS5 streaming installation in Zero. Files folders open directly; row actions are separate and Circle/Back goes to the parent. Cinema Library and Downloads use Store's layout in Cinema colours. New guides: guides/files.md, guides/saved-filters.md, guides/vikingfile.md and guides/stream-install.md.

Vikingfile sign-in in 1.7.0: native App settings → Sources & accounts → Vikingfile, browser App settings → Sources & accounts → Vikingfile, and Zero Settings → Sources & accounts → Vikingfile. PS5 users enter the private account hash on Vikingfile’s official page and select Check sign-in on return. Zero prefills the official form after the user enters the hash locally. Signed in means the provider verified the session, not premium entitlement. Each browser context keeps a separate sign-in. Matching direct links can start without a provider window; human verification remains on the provider page when requested.
